benchmarks.task_description:
Print a provider's plan under the heading an SQL plan has

`ptah schema apply`, its `--dry-run`, `ptah schema plan` and `ptah schema apply --plan` printed a provider's plan under `Planned changes:`, where the built-in YDB engine at 74de0b65b printed `Planned schema changes:` (stokaro/ptah#4204, gap G163). This restores the built-in's wording. Pre-v1, so no compatibility with the earlier output is owed.

## Measurement

YDB 25.1.4.7 and 26.2.1.14, plugin master, a table, a topic, a coordination node and a secret with an input in one directory:

| command | built-in 74de0b65b | master cda568c0d with the provider | this branch with the provider |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `schema apply --dry-run`, `schema apply` | `Planned schema changes:` | `Planned changes:` | `Planned schema changes:` |
| `schema plan --save` | `Planned schema changes:` | `Planned changes:` | `Planned schema changes:` |
| `schema apply --plan <file> --dry-run` | `Planned schema changes:` | `Planned changes:` | `Planned schema changes:` |
| `ptah-compat schema apply` | `Planned schema changes:` | `Planned schema changes:` | `Planned schema changes:` |

The same on both lines. A plan prints the other heading only when it holds a native unit or an approved input (`internal/cli/schema/apply_native.go`, `printPlan` in `plan.go`), and only a provider's plan has either: built-in renderers write SQL units, and execution inputs come from a provider's `DescribeExecutionInputs`. So no built-in engine's output changes, and every printer now reads one constant. The docs already quote `Planned schema changes:` (`direct/apply.md`, `direct/plan-and-approve.md`, `start/choose-a-workflow.md`, `reference/atlas-commands.md`), and none quotes the other heading.

The provider path prints one line the built-in did not: `Execution input: environment PTAH_SECRET_...` above a secret's statement. It states what the built-in left implicit and loses nothing, so it stays.

## Tests

Through the fixture provider in `integration/providercli`: `TestProviderSchemaApplyShowsTheTextForm_HappyPath` and `_FailurePath` expect the heading above a text-form unit and above a native operation in an apply preview, and the new `TestProviderNativePlanFileHeading_HappyPath` expects it from `schema plan` and from `schema apply --plan --dry-run`. Ablation: with the old heading in `apply_native.go` the two preview tests fail, and with it in `printPlan` the plan-file test fails.

The engine-level test is the YDB provider's `TestHostApplyPrintsTheBuiltInsPlanHeading_HappyPath` (stokaro/ptah-ydb-plugin#PLUGINPR, draft, `.github/host-ref` names this branch). It passes with this branch and fails with master on both lines. No other test is owed under `integration/`: the host settles the heading without asking the server.

Checks run: `go test ./internal/cli/schema/`, `go test -tags integration ./integration/providercli -run 'TestProviderSchemaApplyShowsTheTextForm|TestProviderNativePlanFile'`, golangci-lint in both build-tag contours, qtlint, nolintguard, `check-style.mjs`.

diff --git a/integration/providercli/provider_native_plan_file_e2e_test.go b/integration/providercli/provider_native_plan_file_e2e_test.go

--- a/integration/providercli/provider_native_plan_file_e2e_test.go
+++ b/integration/providercli/provider_native_plan_file_e2e_test.go
@@ -96,3 +96,22 @@ func TestProviderNativePlanFileRefusesBeforeWriting(t *testing.T) {
 		})
 	}
 }
+
+// A plan of native operations prints under the heading a plan of SQL text
+// has, whether schema plan saves it or schema apply previews the saved file.
+// The built-in YDB engine printed that heading above every plan, and a plan
+// through a provider is what it planned as SQL.
+func TestProviderNativePlanFileHeading_HappyPath(t *testing.T) {
+	c := qt.New(t)
+	f := nativeCommandFixture(c)
+
+	savedOut, savedNotes, savedCode := f.run(c, c.Context(), "plan", "--schema-file", f.schemaPath, "--output", f.planPath)
+	previewOut, previewNotes, previewCode := f.run(c, c.Context(), "apply", "--plan", f.planPath, "--tx-mode", "none", "--dry-run")
+
+	c.Assert(savedCode, qt.Equals, 0, qt.Commentf("%s", savedNotes))
+	c.Assert(savedOut+savedNotes, qt.Contains, "Planned schema changes:\nNative operation: "+string(operationModel))
+	c.Assert(savedOut+savedNotes, qt.Not(qt.Contains), "Planned changes:")
+	c.Assert(previewCode, qt.Equals, 0, qt.Commentf("%s", previewNotes))
+	c.Assert(previewOut+previewNotes, qt.Contains, "Planned schema changes:\nNative operation: "+string(operationModel))
+	c.Assert(previewOut+previewNotes, qt.Not(qt.Contains), "Planned changes:")
+}

benchmarks.task_description:
Sigenergy: fix grid energy registers

fixes #35242

The grid meter read import energy from register 30562 on the inverter unit, which is reserved in the Sigenergy Modbus protocol v2.9 and returns a constant value. Energy counters now come from the plant unit (247), like the grid power.

- Import energy from plant register 30216 (total imported energy), verified by the reporter on a SigenStor EC
- Export energy added from plant register 30220 (total exported energy)
- Product name corrected to SigenStor EC

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

benchmarks.task_description:
fix(ui): Sync button keeps its size and icon; the header never wraps

Writing in a draft with sync on made the header flicker after each sync. A screen recording shows why: the Sync button's label changed to "Syncing...", the wider button pushed the header past its width, and **Harper Pad**, **Scratch pad**, **Save as file** and the badge all wrapped to two lines until the sync ended.

- The visible label stays "Sync" while a sync runs. The icon turns while it is busy, the accessible name still says "Syncing...", and the status bar says "Syncing...".
- With sync on, the Sync button shows its icon on wide windows too. It was the only header button without one.
- The header never wraps. The no-wrap rule's selector (`.bar .bar > …`) matched nothing, which is why it could. Fixed, and the file name and badge now cut off with an ellipsis. As the window narrows the bar gives up parts in a fixed order: shortcut hints (≤1240px), the brand (≤1040px), then button labels, leaving icons with tooltips (≤1000px). The phone layout (≤720px) is unchanged.

Checked in a browser with a mocked sync server: no wrapping or overflow at any width from 1400px down to 721px, even with an extra 70px item for the update button; the Sync button's width does not change while syncing. Tests, `biome` format and lint pass.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
